statement: The function returns a result r and, for n = len(nums), both of the following hold. (1) For every j with 0 <= j < len(r), the entry r[j] is a permutation of nums: len(r[j]) = n and there exists a bijection pi from {0,...,n-1} to itself such that r[j][i] = nums[pi(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < n. (2) For every sequence p of 64-bit integers that is a permutation of nums (i.e. len(p) = n and p[i] = nums[pi(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < n for some bijection pi from {0,...,n-1} to itself), there is exactly one index j with 0 <= j < len(r) such that len(r[j]) = n and r[j][i] = p[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n. No condition is imposed on the order of the entries r[0],...,r[len(r)-1].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 6; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), nums[i] != nums[j].
